subject.title: feat(gmail): add --inline and --text content modes to gmail attachment

question: Should `gog gmail attachment --text` parse untrusted PDFs in the main CLI process with `github.com/ledongthuc/pdf`, or should PDF extraction be narrowed or isolated before landing?
rationale: Tests, a 3 MiB raw-input cap, and panic recovery do not determine the repository's acceptable CPU, memory, and hang exposure for attacker-controlled email attachments.

options.title: Narrow text mode
options.body: Ship inline, HTML, and plain-text support while deferring PDF extraction until a bounded parser design is approved.

options.title: Bound PDF parsing
options.body: Retain PDF support after adding enforceable isolation or resource limits and adversarial validation.

options.title: Accept in-process parsing
options.body: Land the current parser only as an explicit acceptance of its residual availability exposure.

recommendation.title: Narrow text mode
recommendation.body: Ship inline, HTML, and plain-text support while deferring PDF extraction until a bounded parser design is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: Release ownership and adjacent Gmail command history provide the strongest available routing signal for the new dependency and parser boundary.
